data.content:
# Scoped failure-handling guidance

This guidance supports changes to explicit business rejection branches in [order creation](../../src/orders/create.js), [order cancellation](../../src/orders/cancel.js), and missing-external-ID handling in [shipment reconciliation](../../src/jobs/reconcile.js). It fills the production behavior gap expressly excluded by [existing test guidance](../testing.md). It establishes no service-wide failure policy.

## Order rejection branches

The two checked order operations support a scoped convention of throwing [DomainError](../../src/error.js) for explicit business rejections:

- Creation throws `CUSTOMER_REQUIRED` when `input.customerId` is falsy, with message `An order requires a customer`.
- Creation throws `EMPTY_ORDER` when `input.lines.length === 0`, with message `At least one line is required`.
- Cancellation throws `ALREADY_SHIPPED` when `order.status === 'shipped'`, with message `Shipped orders cannot be cancelled`.

These are two independent operation implementations. The shared error class extends `Error` and stores `code`; it is not another independent operation. This convention covers only the explicit rejection branches checked here, not every runtime failure, other order operations, or future operations by mandate.

## Reconciliation counterexample

[reconcileShipment](../../src/jobs/reconcile.js) returns `{ok: false, reason: 'NO_EXTERNAL_ID'}` when `shipment.externalId` is falsy. This includes absent values but is not an absence-only check.

This single-job local pattern is a counterexample to service-wide throwing. The order operations conversely show that unsuccessful result objects are not universal. No second same-role job was supplied, so no job-wide convention follows. The differing roles do not establish a conflict between explicit policies.

## Suggestions for changes

Suggestion, not existing authority: preserve these branch-specific mechanisms while making a scoped change unless an evidenced decision authorizes different behavior. Treat converting throws to result objects, converting reconciliation results to throws, or changing rejection codes as behavior decisions requiring caller evidence. This suggestion does not standardize either mechanism.

Suggestion, not existing authority: before changing failure mechanisms, inspect the affected callers and adapters, relevant tests, other jobs, scheduling configuration, and retry policies. Those sources were not supplied here. How failures propagate or translate, whether scheduling reacts to returned failures, and whether retries occur remain unresolved. `NO_EXTERNAL_ID` cannot be classified from this evidence as retryable, permanent, or skipped work.

## Existing authorities

Use [docs/testing.md](../testing.md) for test invocation authority in its original scope. This document neither replaces that guidance nor claims that tests ran or passed; test coverage and outcomes were not supplied.

Native OpenSpec authority remains in the original [explore](../../.agents/skills/openspec-explore/SKILL.md), [propose](../../.agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md), [update](../../.agents/skills/openspec-update-change/SKILL.md), [apply](../../.agents/skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md), [sync](../../.agents/skills/openspec-sync-specs/SKILL.md), and [archive](../../.agents/skills/openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md) workflows. Their human gates, planning boundaries, blocked states, full task completion criteria, selected-sync checks, validation, post-sync comparisons, and archive warnings and choices remain governed there. This research does not alter or satisfy any of them and supplies no historical approval or check result.

Only the supplied filtered evidence was assessed. These source gaps do not prove that policies or additional guidance are absent elsewhere in the repository.
